did: Recorded the settings scope census (3 rows, all all_users) and the admin account set (test.admin) as fixture data
Captured the twelve retired role lists verbatim, with administrator and Setup Tech recorded as matching no catalogue role
Added first_name, last_name and temporary_credential_failed_attempts to core_users_profiles; scratch-database run proved the guarded rollback drops exactly those three
Added role_rank INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with an index to auth_roles_catalog; longest index name 31 characters
Created auth_user_management_audit at 32_ with the 12 declared columns and no foreign keys, so the actor snapshots outlive the accounts they name
Re-ranked fn_config_settings_scope_rank to computer 1, all_users 2, role 3, admin 4, developer 5, user 6; scratch-database run read back 1,2,3,4,5,6 and the rollback restored 1,2,3,4,5 with role 0

Added role_code and the wrong-attempt count to the three credential reads, plus the upper-case sign-in-name contract in their headers; all three recreate and return the documented ordinal order against a scratch store

Added sp_auth_temporary_credential_attempt_record (one statement per branch, non-query) and the header comment on sp_config_settings_upsert recording why it is not the permission write path and why ELSE 'developer' stays

Added the roster read (four-field search, optional role filter, everyone and switched-off people by default) and the one-person read returning identity, rung, active flag and attempt count; both exercised against a scratch store

Added the create procedure: one transaction writing profile plus exactly one role assignment; proved rank refusal, unknown-role refusal, pass-through 1062 and eight audit rows sharing one change group

Added the update procedure: target-rank refusal checked before the requested-role refusal, self-deactivate and self-rename refusals, and audit rows only for fields that actually changed (nothing-changed wrote none)

Added the reset procedure: stores the salted hash only, forces a change, clears the attempt count, leaves is_active as it was, ends no session, and writes one audit row with both value columns null; target-rank refusal and a null-value audit row both proved

Added sp_config_permissions_user_get keyed on scope_key, resolving the role inside the procedure and returning only permission-namespace rows; proved it returns the person's own row and their role's row and excludes another role's baseline and a text preference

Added the sign-in-name upper-case migration with a recorded backup table its rollback restores then drops; proved against a scratch store that it upper-cases, records one row, reports rather than fails, and that the rollback restored the original spelling
